title: Trump’s Tactics to Lower Beef Prices and Appease Ranchers Fall Short
partialText: The Agriculture Department offered new initiatives for ranchers after President Trump said he would import more beef. The moves aren’t a quick fix.

title: Chevron Expansion in Venezuela Extends U.S. Influence Over Oil Riches
partialText: The U.S. energy giant, which stayed in the country after other Western companies left, will invest $7 billion in the country to more than double its production there.

title: Investors Still on Edge Over War, Debt and Inflation
partialText: U.S. and Iranian forces traded attacks again, pushing oil prices higher, stocks lower and making bond investors nervous.

title: Employer Health Costs Are Expected to Spike in 2027
partialText: A new U.S. survey anticipates an average increase of 11 percent unless benefits are cut, the highest rate in decades. Other findings also predict a sharp rise.

title: Global Bond Rates Are Rising. What Should You Do Now?
partialText: If you own bonds, they may be in a broad fund that hasn’t lost much money. And that fund may do much better in the next several years.

title: FiveThirtyEight’s Podcast Hosts Reunite for a New Show
partialText: Nate Silver, Clare Malone and Galen Druke will host “Still Counting,” a nonpartisan politics show — on a decidedly partisan podcast network.

title: Saturday Evening Post Will Stop Printing After 205 Years
partialText: The magazine, famous for publishing Jack London stories and Norman Rockwell art, will continue online.

title: Get to Know Your Phone’s Built-In Emergency Kit
partialText: In times of natural disasters and other dangers, special features tucked away on your iPhone or Android device could help make a difference.

title: Inside the Fight Against a Flesh-Eating Fly in Mexico
partialText: For the first time in a year, the U.S.-Mexico border partly reopened to cattle imports following a screwworm infestation across the region. The battle against the flesh-eating fly has only just begun deep in Mexico.

title: Missouri Voters Appear to Recall City Councilman Over Data Center Support
partialText: Initial results showed that residents of Independence, Mo., voted overwhelmingly to recall an official who backed billions of dollars in tax breaks for a data center.

title: Bill Simmons’s Co-Hosts Are Tired of His A.I. Antics
partialText: The founder of The Ringer is taking flak for using artificial intelligence to conjure opinions from the deceased film critic Roger Ebert. Ads from OpenAI have recently run on the show.

title: What to Know About Venezuelan Energy Following Trump’s Oil Deal
partialText: The Trump administration’s deal with a private oil company to increase oil production in the South American country could take many years to come to fruition.

title: Two More Oil Tankers Are Attacked in the Strait of Hormuz
partialText: The ships were hit near Oman on Monday, the latest attacks on vessels in the Persian Gulf. Oil prices rose more than 2 percent.

title: At G20 Meeting, Scott Bessent Accuses China of Flooding the World With Cheap Exports
partialText: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent accused China for flooding the world with its cheap exports.

title: Ozempic Maker Novo Nordisk’s Investors Are Nervously Looking Into the Future
partialText: Novo Nordisk’s chief executive, Mike Doustdar, is a year into a corporate turnaround. He says investors are still underestimating the promise of the company’s drugs.

title: Satsuki Katayama, the Woman at the Center of Japan’s Currency Fight
partialText: Japan’s finance minister, Satsuki Katayama, is under pressure to strengthen the yen while balancing competing demands from the prime minister and Washington.

title: Bond Sell-Off Threatens to Squeeze Borrowers Around the World
partialText: Government bond yields are hitting multi-decade highs, reflecting anxiety about debt levels, deficits and inflation. The effects will extend to mortgages, business loans and other types of credit.

title: How the Pentagon Is Getting Into the Venezuelan Oil Business Under Trump
partialText: The Defense Department’s Office of Strategic Capital, founded by the Biden administration to give loans to bolster the U.S. defense industry, is helping lead President Trump’s oil deal.

title: Shein’s Lackluster Debut Shows a Fast-Fashion Model Left Behind
partialText: Squeezed by new trade rules, shrinking market share and labor concerns, Shein’s share decline in Hong Kong on Tuesday is a sign investors have moved on.

title: Donald Trump Jr.’s Firm Leads $1 Billion Funding Round for Polymarket
partialText: The new round values the prediction market at $21 billion, up from $15 billion. Mr. Trump’s firm, 1789 Capital, will invest around $300 million.

title: Expedia Fights Off Claim for Damages by Cuban Exile Families
partialText: A jury in Florida found that in their suit against the travel booking company, the plaintiffs had failed to prove ownership over tourism properties in Cuba.

title: IRS Audit Revenue Has Plummeted Under Trump, Watchdog Finds
partialText: The I.R.S. lost roughly a quarter of its employees since President Trump took office, hampering the agency’s ability to conduct audits.

title: Kalshi Permanently Bars George Santos From the Platform
partialText: The prediction market said it had barred George Santos, the former congressman from New York, and fined him $71,356 over evidence he engaged in insider trading.

title: Private Equity Wants to Invest in College Sports. Some Schools Are Wary.
partialText: As desperate as many athletic programs are for money, they are proceeding cautiously when it comes to deals with private equity.

title: U.S. Start-Up and Saudi Arabia Form Data Center Partnership
partialText: Together AI, which serves open-source artificial intelligence models, announced a deal to use compute from Humain in Saudi Arabia, where it can bypass U.S. backlash over data centers.

title: Global Oil Price Rises to $90 a Barrel After U.S. and Iran Trade Attacks
partialText: The first attacks in a month jolted energy markets. The average U.S. gasoline price remained 37 percent higher since the war began.

title: Europe Protests as U.S. Invites Russian Minister to G20 Finance Meeting
partialText: The meeting, which China and Russia are attending, is focused on the ongoing economic shock from the war in Iran, which has driven up oil prices globally.

title: A $480,000-a-Year Pill Reflects a New Normal for Cancer Drugs
partialText: Rasonque, the new pancreatic cancer treatment from Revolution Medicines, illustrates the huge inflation in cancer drug prices over the past two decades.

title: A Half-Price Luxury E.V. Comes With a Big Asterisk
partialText: The Polestar 4 is a solid car, and current incentives make it a bargain. But the company, a Chinese-owned brand, is being forced from the U.S. market.

title: Chinese Cars Could Be Huge in U.S., and That’s the Problem, Officials Say
partialText: The Times test-drove a stunning crossover from Geely that would cost under half of what its rivals charge. Two senators and many experts point to security and economic concerns as reasons for a ban.

title: U.A.E. To Review Banque Misr, Targeted by Iran Sanctions
partialText: The Treasury Department accused Banque Misr’s branches in the United Arab Emirates of helping Iran. The Emirati central bank promised an examination.

title: A Mortgage Servicer Sent a Letter About an Address Change. Was It Deed Theft?
partialText: A letter arrived in the mail from PNC Bank about an address change on a mortgage account. Was a deed theft scheme in process?

title: The Case of the Truly Incorrigible Cubicle Yakker
partialText: Plus: Is it normal to video-interview for a job while the hiring panel’s cameras are all off?

title: Help Wanted: ‘Forward-Deployed’ Humans for the A.I. Era
partialText: Start-ups are using the military-derived term to glorify customer-facing work as clients seek people to help set up artificial intelligence tools.

title: Pennsylvania Gambling Addicts Hope that ‘Skill Games’ Will Go Bust
partialText: The machines, which enjoyed legal protection until a recent court ruling, could go dark in October.

title: Trump’s Venezuelan Oil Deal Relies on a Powerful and Divisive Partner
partialText: The administration will work with a private Venezuelan oil company that has close ties to the country’s government.

title: Treasury Bars Some Reporters From G20 Finance Meeting
partialText: Specific reporters from The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal and Bloomberg were not granted credentials to cover the meeting of financial leaders next week in Asheville, N.C.

title: Warsh, After Talking Tough on Inflation, Faces a ‘No-Win Situation’ on Rates
partialText: Kevin M. Warsh, the chairman of the Federal Reserve, must soon decide whether to raise interest rates if inflation does not ease, even if it draws President Trump’s ire.

title: 40,000 Pounds of Pabst Blue Ribbon Beer Reported Stolen in California
partialText: The company responded to the theft by setting a deadline for the return of the product. “P.S., this is real and we are deadly serious,” it said on social media.

title: Teleprompter Operator Who Bet on Trump Speeches Is Ordered to Pay Fine
partialText: Gabriel Perez had access to the president’s speeches before they were delivered and was accused of placing unlawful wagers on words that would be spoken.

title: Thievery or Innovation? The Music Industry Grapples With A.I.
partialText: Some labels have sued A.I. music generators like Suno. Others have partnered with them. At least one has done both.

title: As Deadly Flash Flooding Batters Nepal, Some Fear ‘the Entire Himalayas Are Melting’
partialText: A glacier unleashed a deadly flood earlier this week. For local trekking guides and climbers, the mountains were already changing.

title: Catastrophic Flood Exposes the Risks of Nepal’s Hydropower Bet
partialText: The loss of power-generating capacity has raised questions about an ambitious expansion of renewable energy in one of the world’s most hazard-prone mountain regions.

title: High Debt and Rising Prices Catch Up to Trump, as Midterms Near
partialText: To win in 2024, the president promised an economic course correction. Almost two years later, his agenda has made that fight even harder.

title: “The Invisible Hand of Maria Edgeworth”: An Economist, Erased
partialText: Maria Edgeworth sneaked economic theory into her best-selling novels. Two centuries later, a new book finally gives her the credit she deserves.

title: Walmart to Pay $50 Million to Settle Opioid Lawsuit, US Says
partialText: The resolution is part of an effort to hold retailers and pharmacists accountable for what the government says were their roles in the opioid epidemic.

title: Trump Says U.S. Struck Deal for Control of More Than 65 Billion Barrels of Venezuela’s Oil
partialText: The president said an agreement between the countries covered more than 65 billion barrels of reserves. A U.S. official said it would involve a partnership with a private company.

title: Prediction Markets Should Be Regulated as Gambling, Appeals Court Says
partialText: The outcome contradicted an earlier appeals court decision. Federal regulators said the split rulings called for resolution by the Supreme Court.

title: Chevron Is in Talks to Expand in Venezuela, a Potential Win for Trump
partialText: President Trump’s administration has been pushing U.S. companies like Chevron to invest more in Venezuela’s oil industry.

title: Trump Updates $15 Billion Libel Lawsuit Against The New York Times
partialText: The president has argued that the news organization sought to undermine his 2024 presidential campaign by disparaging his reputation as a businessman. The Times has moved to dismiss the lawsuit.
